ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a schematic geological section of a certain place. Near the ground surface in the upper left part, it is marked “A,” and the top is also marked with positions B, C, D, etc.; the legend shows that the section contains rock layers or geological bodies such as limestone, granite, iron ore body, drilling, sandstone, and glutenite. The figure itself mainly provides the position marker “A”; the landscape judgment mainly combines the river flow direction, bank erosion, and time information in the stem. Then reason: The stem says that at site A there is a river flowing from south to north, and the west bank is more heavily eroded. When a river flows north, if it is in the Northern Hemisphere, under the influence of the geostrophic deflection force, it should deflect to the right, and the right bank, namely the east bank, is more strongly eroded; now the west bank is more heavily eroded, indicating that the direction of motion deflects to the left, which conforms to the characteristics of the Southern Hemisphere, so this place is in the Southern Hemisphere. Also, because at 18:50 Beijing time the shadow of the local flagpole shrank to a point, it indicates that the Sun is directly overhead locally, and the local time at this moment is 12:00 noon, so this place is in the tropics between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn. Beijing time uses the local time at 120°E. 18:50 is 6 hours 50 minutes later than local noon 12:00. A time difference of 6 hours 50 minutes corresponds to a longitude difference of about 102.5°. The local time is later than Beijing, so it is west of Beijing, with a longitude of about 120°E－102.5°＝17.5°E. 17.5°E and located in the tropics of the Southern Hemisphere roughly correspond to the Namib area in southwestern Africa. Affected by the subtropical high and cold current, etc., the typical landscape may be a tropical desert landscape.
